results.commodity_narrative:
School bottling orders continue to draw upon milk volumes available for cheese processing. Unseasonably warm weather has affected some states in the Northeast, and contacts say that this has stalled seasonal increases in milk production. Cheese production is steady, though some contacts say that cheese demand and orders from customers are down in contrast to the healthy demand over the summer months. Cheddar and mozzarella continue to be the most in-demand American and Italian-type cheeses, respectively. Last week's National Retail Report lists shredded cheese in 6-8-ounce packages as the most advertised conventional cheese item, with a national weighted average advertised price of $2.46, down from $2.54 last week. In the Northeast U.S., the weighted average advertised price of shredded cheese in  6-8-ounce packages is listed at $2.56. Market prices for cheese blocks on industry cash exchanges closed at $1.8000 last Wednesday but slid to $1.7575 as of report publishing time. In the Northeast, wholesale prices for cheddar and muenster are down $0.0800 and process cheese prices are down $0.1850. Grade A Swiss prices are unchanged.

NOTICE: Due to evolving market conditions, collection and publication of the Northeast Wholesale Selling Prices, Delivered, for 1,000 - 5,000 lbs mixed lots will end with Report 39, during the week of September 25, 2023. Questions and comments regarding this termination plan can be directed to: Janet.Linder@ams.usda.gov, (608)422-8588.

results.commodity_narrative:
Strong milk volumes continue to clear into Class I operations, as school bottling orders remain steady. As a result, volumes of milk that were previously available for Class III operations continue to be lower. Cooler temperatures both during the day and at night have reached the East coast, and contacts suggest that upticks in milk production may be on the horizon. Cheese processing continues to be limited by persistent labor obstacles, as well as limited milk volumes. Contacts note demand for cheddar is the strongest of the American-type cheeses, and mozzarella continues to be in high demand due to steady foodservice orders. Retail demand remains strong. Last week's National Retail Report lists shredded cheese in 6-8-ounce packages as the most advertised conventional cheese item, with a national weighted average advertised price of $2.54, up from $2.49 last week. In the Northeast U.S., the weighted average advertised price of shredded cheese in 6-8-ounce packages is $2.25. Market prices for cheese blocks on industry cash exchanges closed at $1.91 last Wednesday but fell to $1.88 as of report publishing time. In the Northeast, wholesale prices for cheddar and muenster are down $0.05 and process cheese prices are up $0.04. Grade A Swiss prices are unchanged.

NOTICE: Due to evolving market conditions, collection and publication of the Northeast Wholesale Selling Prices, Delivered, for 1,000 - 5,000 lbs mixed lots will end with Report 39, during the week of September 25, 2023. Questions and comments regarding this termination plan can be directed to: Janet.Linder@ams.usda.gov, (608)422-8588.

results.commodity_narrative:
Several school districts in the Northeast returned for the first day of the semester only after Labor Day weekend. As a result, the amount of milk clearing into Class I operations continues to draw upon milk volumes for Class III manufacturing. Some cheese plant managers suggest labor issues persist, and manufacturing was paused due to plant downtime over the holiday weekend. American-type cheeses like cheddar are a main production focus. Demand for process American and mozzarella is strong, namely on the school-meal foodservice front. Demand for cheese from the restaurant sector is steady, and cheese demand in retail settings is strong. Last week's National Retail Report lists sliced cheese in 6-8-ounce packages as the most advertised conventional cheese item, with a weighted average advertised price of $2.27, up from $2.19 last week. In the Northeast, the weighted average advertised price of sliced cheese in 6-8-ounce packages is $2.31. Market prices for cheese blocks on industry cash exchanges closed at $1.9925 last Wednesday but slid to $1.9500 as of report publishing time. In the Northeast, wholesale prices for cheddar and muenster are up $0.0275 and process cheese prices are up $0.0450. Grade A Swiss prices are down $0.1375.

NOTICE: Due to evolving market conditions, collection and publication of the Northeast Wholesale Selling Prices, Delivered, for 1,000 - 5,000 lbs mixed lots will end with Report 39, during the week of September 25, 2023. Some cheese plant managers have also relayed that persistent labor issues have affected how much milk they are taking in and therefore the amount of cheese they are able to manufacture. Despite labor obstacles, cheese inventories are said to be steady. Contacts say that cheddar continues to be in higher demand than other American-type cheeses, and that demand for mozzarella from food service customers is strong. Last week's National Retail Report lists that shredded cheese in 6-8-ounce packages was the most advertised conventional cheese item this week, with a weighted average advertised price of $2.45, down 5 cents from last week. Market prices for cheese blocks on industry cash exchanges closed at $2.0175 last Wednesday but fell to $1.9475 as of report publishing time. In the Northeast, wholesale prices for cheddar and muenster are up $0.0450 and process cheese prices are up $0.0075. Grade A Swiss prices are unchanged.
results.secondary_source_info: This week, a cooperative export assistance program accepted requests for export assistance on contracts to sell 1.3 million (573 metric tons) of American-type cheese and 187,000 pounds (85 metric tons) of cream cheese. results.commodity_narrative: Milk volumes are flat in the Northeast. Contacts have shared that cooler nighttime temperatures have improved farm level milk volumes relative to recent weeks. As schools reopen, bottling orders have increased, and the volume of milk going into processing plants has declined. Cheese plant managers have relayed that labor issues and decreased milk volumes going into processing have slowed cheese production. Contacts have also shared that cheddar continues to be in higher demand than other American-type cheeses and that mozzarella demand from food service customers is strong. Cheese demand in retail stores is steady, with last week's National Retail Report listing that conventional cheese ads increased by 35 percent from the week prior and that shredded cheese in 6-8-ounce packages was the most advertised conventional cheese item, with a weighted average advertised price of $2.50, down 18 cents from last week. Market prices for cheese blocks on industry cash exchanges closed at $1.9650 last Wednesday and rose to $2.0150 as of report publishing time. In the Northeast, wholesale prices for cheddar and muenster are up $0.01, but process cheese prices are down $0.0375. Grade A Swiss prices are unchanged.

Market prices for cheese blocks on industry cash exchanges closed at $1.40 last Wednesday and dropped to $1.31 as of report publishing time. results.secondary_source_info:
The NASS Cold Storage report evidenced that May 2023 cheese stocks were up 1 percent from April 2023 but down 1 percent from May 2022. 

This week, a cooperative export assistance program accepted requests for export assistance on contracts to sell 461,000 pounds (209 metric tons) of American-type cheese and 271,000 pounds (123 metric tons) of cream cheese. So far this year, the program has assisted member cooperatives who have contracts to sell 24 million pounds of American-type cheeses and 4.4 million pounds of cream cheese in export markets.

results.commodity_narrative:
Milk volumes are steady in the Northeast, and there are strong volumes clearing into Class III operations.  Contacts have shared that cheese demand is quiet in contrast to ample available inventories. Retail demand is unchanged, while food service demand remains quiet as some consumers continue to be dissuaded by menu price inflation. Contacts have relayed that some customers are opting to put cheese into longer term storage spaces. Plant managers report that production of American-type cheese is strong, and that Swiss and Italian-type inventories are steady. Market prices for cheese blocks on industry cash exchanges dipped down to $1.42 last Wednesday and have increased to $1.46 as of report time. In the Northeast, wholesale prices for cheddar and muenster are down $0.1200, and process cheese prices are down $0.0025 from last week. Grade A Swiss prices are up $0.0375.

The DMN May monthly average price for Swiss was $4.6589 compared to $4.8338 one month ago. For 40-pound blocks of cheddar, the monthly average was $2.2169 compared to $2.4444 last month. Process American had a monthly average price of $1.8557, compared to $2.0313 one month ago. Muenster had a monthly average price of $2.2357, up from $2.4631 one month ago.
results.secondary_source_info: The CME Group May monthly average price for barrels was $1.5073, compared to $1.5921 one month ago; the monthly average price for blocks was $1.5719, compared to $1.7574 one month ago.

Fluid milk volumes are steadily clearing into Class III operations and production of American-type and Italian-type cheeses is strong. Inventories of American-type cheeses like cheddar and Colby are increasing. Cream cheese production is seasonally steady. Market contacts have shared that food service demand has quieted some as restaurant prices remain high, whereas retail demand is steady to stronger. Market prices for cheese blocks on industry cash exchanges reached $1.6425 last Wednesday and closed at $1.6625 as of reporting. In the Northeast, wholesale prices for cheddar and muenster are down 8.75 cents while process cheese prices are up half a cent from last week. Grade A Swiss prices are unchanged this week. 
The DMN April monthly average price for Swiss was $4.8338 compared to $4.9313 one month ago. For 40-pound blocks of cheddar, the monthly average was $2.4444 compared to $2.5370 last month. Process American had a monthly average price of $2.0313, compared to $2.0861 one month ago. Muenster had a monthly average price of $2.4631, up from $2.5558 one month ago.

results.secondary_source_info:

Milk is available for cheese makers to run busy production schedules throughout the Northeast. Some plant managers report labor shortages and delayed deliveries of production supplies are preventing them from running at or near capacity. A cold front moved into the region earlier this week and some contacts anticipate that subzero temperatures will have a negative impact on milk availability for cheese production. Market prices for cheese blocks on the CME reached $1.8950 on Wednesday of last week and have declined by 6 cents to $1.8350 as of reporting. Some stakeholders suggest growing cheese inventories are contributing to declining market prices. Retail demand for cheese is softening, while contacts relay mixed food service sales. Food service demand for cheddar cheese is, reportedly, lighter, though sales of pizza and mozzarella cheese remain strong ahead of the professional football championship game. 

In the Northeast, wholesale cheese prices for both cheddar and Muenster are down $0.0850, and process cheese prices are down $0.0150. Grade A Swiss prices are down $0.0900 this week.

The CME Group November monthly average price for barrels was $1.9454, compared to $2.1285 one month ago; blocks' average price was $2.1186, compared to $2.0260 one month ago.

This week, a cooperative export assistance program accepted requests for export assistance on contracts to sell 1.6 million pounds (734 metric tons) of American-type cheese and 717,000 pounds (325 metric tons) of cream cheese. So far this year, the program has assisted member cooperatives who have contracts to sell 92.1 million pounds of American-type cheeses and 8.8 million pounds of cream cheese in export markets.
results.methodology: Information for the period December 5 - 9, 2022, issued weekly

results.commodity_narrative:
Milk production is steady in the Northeast, meeting some producers' seasonal expectations. Cheesemakers say they are utilizing available volumes of milk to run active production schedules. Some plant managers say labor shortages and delayed deliveries of production supplies persist and are preventing them from operating full schedules. Retail demand for cheese is strong as some grocers are restocking in preparation for end of year holidays. Meanwhile, food service demand for cheese is unchanged. Stakeholders say export demand is softening. Cheese loads remain available for purchasing on the spot market.

In the Northeast, wholesale cheese prices for both cheddar and Muenster are down $0.0875, but process cheese prices are up $0.0250. Grade A Swiss prices are down $0.0300 this week.

Milk is available for cheese makers to run active production schedules in the Northeast. Some cheesemakers are operating below capacity due to labor shortages and delayed deliveries of production supplies. Demand for cheese is steady from both retail and food service customers. Some stakeholders say cheese prices are declining in international markets and having a negative impact on export demand. The NASS Cold Storage report released on November 22, 2022, showed total natural cheese stocks were down 1 percent from September and only slightly below October 2021 levels. Spot purchasers say this data was in line with expectations as cheese has remained available on the spot market.

In the Northeast, wholesale cheese prices for both cheddar and Muenster are down $0.0425, and process cheese prices are down $0.1875. Grade A Swiss prices are unchanged this week.

results.commodity_narrative:
Farm level production continues its seasonal decline, but milk abounds for Class III operations. Regional cheese production is steady. Inventories are hearty, with some market participants voicing concerns that supply may be outpacing demand. Softer retail sales persist. Contacts say some retailers are reducing orders and/or streamlining product offerings. Food service demand remains level to lower. Recent reports suggest costly business lunches are becoming less common. Some data indicate business lunch spending is down in cities including New York City, Philadelphia, and Washington, DC. Hybrid workweeks are necessitating other means of connection. Furthermore, in the face of high input costs and staffing shortages, some restauranteurs are discontinuing lower-priced lunch specials or choosing to close during lunch hours. 

In the Northeast, wholesale cheese prices for both cheddar and Muenster are down $0.0150, and process cheese prices decreased $0.0375. Grade A Swiss prices are unchanged this week.

results.commodity_narrative:
Strong milk flows are clearing to Class III operations. For some plants, production schedules have been impacted by holiday downtime, labor pool issues, and/or supply chain shortages. Overall, however, cheesemaking remains generally active across the region. Manufacturers' inventories are bountiful, and cheese is reportedly available for spot and contract purchasing. While export interest continues to demonstrate strength, some market participants relay softening domestic demand across sectors. Retail sales are down as consumers face inflationary price pressures at the point of sale. Food service orders are weaker as well. On the CME this Tuesday, when the holiday-shortened trading week opened, prices for both blocks and barrels dropped. The block and barrel price relationship is, once again, inverted.

In the Northeast, wholesale cheese prices for both cheddar and Muenster are up $0.0625, and process cheese prices increased $0.0150. Grade A Swiss prices are up $0.2250 this week.

The DMN Northeast June 2022 monthly average price for cheddar blocks is $2.8199, compared to $2.9436 one month ago. Processed 5# sliced average price is $2.5738, compared to $2.7065 one month ago.

results.commodity_narrative:
Steady milk supplies are clearing to Class III operations. Production is busy for Northeastern cheesemakers. However, operating capacity for some cheesemaking plants is challenged by ongoing labor pool issues and shortages of trucks/drivers and production/packaging supplies. Additionally, a recent blast of wintery weather reportedly caused hazardous road conditions, contributing to some delivery delays. Cheese inventories are plentiful. U.S. prices are competitive on export markets, and global cheese demand is tenacious. Stateside, cheese sales are firm to higher, as well. Retail sales are good. Food service demand is stable to growing as the restaurant sector continues its rebound. Retail sales are good. On the CME this week through Tuesday, block and barrel price movement has been, cumulatively, downward. Despite this, Tuesday's prices remain above last week's average prices, and the inversion of the block and barrel price relationship persists. 

In the Northeast, wholesale cheese prices for both cheddar and Muenster are up $0.0425, and process cheese prices increased $0.0875. Grade A Swiss prices are unchanged this week.

results.commodity_narrative:
Class III milk intakes are strong as milk output slowly increases. Despite staffing shortages and supply chain interruptions of some production/packaging materials, Northeastern cheese plant managers are maintaining robust production schedules. Regional inventories are abundant, although market participants say steadily strong demand keeps supply levels manageable. Export interest is good; U.S. cheese prices remain favorable on global markets. Across domestic sectors, cheese sales are trending stable to stronger. Hearty demand is present from retail customers, and food service orders are steady to higher. On the CME, the block and barrel price relationship inverted last week as spot prices for both pushed past the $2.30 mark. Prices have held firm through Tuesday of this week.

In the Northeast, wholesale cheese prices for both cheddar and Muenster are up $0.0625, and process cheese prices increased $0.0900. Grade A Swiss prices are unchanged this week.

Milk production continues to increase, and steady supplies are clearing to Northeastern Class III operations. Plant managers are keeping active cheese production schedules. Some dairy processing facilities continue to navigate labor issues, transportation bottlenecks, and/or supply shortages. Despite such challenges, cheese output is strong and regional inventories are sturdy. Export interest is reportedly good as global milk supplies remain tighter and U.S. cheese prices are favorable on international markets. Market participants report healthy cheese demand across domestic sectors as well. Retail sales are unchanged. While some variation exists from one locale to another, food service sales are generally level to improving. 

In the Northeast, wholesale cheese prices for both cheddar and Muenster are up $0.0100, and process cheese prices increased $0.0350. Grade A Swiss prices are up $0.2250 this week.

The DMN Northeast March 2022 monthly average price for cheddar blocks is $2.7156, compared to $2.4798 one month ago. Processed 5# sliced average price is $2.3608, compared to $2.1886 one month ago.

results.commodity_narrative:
Northeastern cheese manufacturers are maintaining busy production schedules. Class III milk intakes are steady to increasing. Some cheesemaking plants are operating near capacity despite delivery delays, supply issues, and staffing shortages that continue to challenge dairy processing operations. Regional cheese inventories are plentiful. Industry contacts suggest sustained good demand prevents hearty supplies from becoming too onerous. U.S. cheese prices remain competitive on global markets, and export interest is robust. Domestic sales are stable to higher. Food service orders are steadily strong. Market participants say some limited-service eateries are meeting or surpassing pre-pandemic business levels, which is correlated with a boost in cheese consumption. Retail sales are unchanged; customer demand remains strong. 

In the Northeast, wholesale cheese prices for both cheddar and Muenster are up $0.1075, and process cheese prices increased $0.1650. Grade A Swiss prices are unchanged this week.

Steady milk supplies are flowing to Northeastern cheese manufacturers. Production is fairly active for cheddar, mozzarella, and provolone. However, some cheesemaking facilities are operating under capacity as plant managers contend with labor pool issues, shortages of production/packaging supplies, and transportation delays. Additionally, winter storm-related road closures have, in recent weeks, disrupted hauling routes and prevented some staff from getting to plants. Regional cheese supplies are plentiful. Inventories are available to meet current spot and contract needs. Retail demand has been receiving a boost ahead of an upcoming major sporting event this weekend. results.commodity_narrative:
Milk is available for Northeastern Class III operations. Milk intakes for some cheesemaking facilities are at or near capacity. Plant managers are working to keep busy cheese production schedules throughout the region despite the challenges of staffing shortages, supply chain issues, and winter weather-related transportation delays. Cheese inventories are available for spot needs. Retail demand is sturdy as the end of the football season approaches. Food service orders are a little mixed. Sales from educational institutions are steadying. However, there are reportedly pockets of softening restaurant demand as dine-in traffic in some areas has wavered in recent weeks. On the CME Tuesday, both cheddar block and barrel prices dipped lower, but the block and barrel price spread remained inverted. 

In the Northeast, wholesale cheese prices for both cheddar and Muenster are down $0.0175, but process cheese prices increased $0.0650. Grade A Swiss prices are unchanged this week.

However, orders are wavering in some locales where dine-in service is limited by staffing shortages, temporary COVID-related closures, and safety restrictions. Retail demand is steady to stronger. Through Tuesday of this week on the CME group, barrel and cheddar block prices pushed upward.

Some market participants suggest that recent reports of the Omicron variant have not, so far, deterred restaurant patrons from dining out. Food service sales are firm. Retail cheese orders are stable following last week’s holiday. Through Tuesday of this week, barrel prices climbed higher on the CME Group while block prices are unchanged.  

In the Northeast, the wholesale cheese prices for both cheddar and Muenster are up $0.1350, and the process cheese prices increased $0.0400. The Grade A Swiss prices are unchanged this week.

results.commodity_narrative:
Northeastern cheesemakers are receiving adequate milk supplies to support strong cheddar, mozzarella, and provolone production. Regional cheese stocks are plentiful, but some contacts believe inventories are in good balance with hearty customer demand. November retail cheese sales are showing quiet growth month to month. As shoppers prepare for at-home holiday feasts and other seasonal get togethers, some grocers continue to heavily promote cheese specials in weekly advertisements. Cheese demand from the food service sector is reportedly somewhat mixed, but the overall trend is steady. To start off the shortened holiday week, block prices held firm Monday on the CME Group while barrel prices shifted lower. Market participants are curious to see where spot prices will go as the calendar moves through the holiday season. 

In the Northeast, the wholesale cheese prices for both cheddar and Muenster are down $0.0225, and the process cheese prices decreased $0.0525. The Grade A Swiss prices are unchanged this week.

Regional inventories are hearty but cheese stocks are reportedly well-balanced with customer demands. Food service cheese sales are steady to stronger. Retail demand is increasing. Some grocers are placing additional cheese orders and featuring cheese promotions in weekly advertisements. Some market participants believe that supply chain issues, driver shortages, and delivery delays may be contributing factors to recent price swings and market volatility. Despite these challenges, however, and at least for the near term, other contacts feel that cheese markets have a bullish undertone.     

In the Northeast, the wholesale cheese prices for both cheddar and Muenster are up $0.1100. However, the process cheese prices decreased $0.0700. The Grade A Swiss prices are unchanged this week.

results.commodity_narrative:
Cheese markets are holding a stable market undertone. In the Northeast, milk volumes are available for Class III productions. Cheddar cheese operations are receiving a heavy milk supply for strong production schedules. Additionally, mozzarella and provolone cheese makers are working on full production for their immediate needs. Regional cheese inventory levels are balanced with customers’ demands. Cheese demands are fairly healthy in the retail and restaurant sectors. Supply chain/transportation challenges continue to impact many dairy products and the industry. Block and barrel cheese prices on the CME Group are currently closing around the $1.60s. 

In the Northeast, the wholesale cheese prices for both cheddar and Muenster are down $0.0150. However, the process cheese prices increased $0.0125. The Grade A Swiss prices are unchanged this week.  

The DMN Northeast October 2021 monthly average price for cheddar blocks is $2.3808, compared to $2.3501 one month ago. Processed 5# sliced average price is $2.1043, compared to $1.8261 one month ago.
results.secondary_source_info:
The CME Group October 2021 monthly average price for barrels was $1.8008, compared to $1.5319 a month ago; blocks’ average price was $1.7798, up from $1.7601 a month ago.

This week, a cooperative export assistance program accepted requests for export assistance to sell 154,000 pounds (70 MT) cheese and 736,000 pounds (334 MT) of cream cheese.

Educational institutions’ meal options are limited in numerous areas, as some manufacturers are not able to deliver orders or fulfill immediate needs. The block and barrel cheese price relationship on CME Group trading is currently inverted, with the barrel price above that of the block price.  

In the Northeast, the wholesale cheese prices for both cheddar and Muenster are down $0.0200. However, the process cheese prices increased $0.0550. The Grade A Swiss prices are unchanged this week.

results.commodity_narrative:
At the end of June, cheese manufacturers are receiving a substantial supply of milk loads. Mozzarella and provolone production schedules are full. Cheddar cheese output is strong with production operating near/at capacity. Some cheese manufacturers are working through the holiday. Regional inventory levels are fairly available for spot/contract agreements. On the CME Group, barrel cheese pricing is mixed, while block cheese pricing is near the low $1.50s currently. Cheese sales in the retail sector are stable to a bit higher. Some grocery stores are promoting additional cheese ads for the holiday. Foodservice sales vary. Some restaurants are purchasing regular cheese supplies, while other restaurants have limited purchases.   

In the Northeast, the wholesale cheese prices for both cheddar and Muenster decreased $0.0175. In addition, the process cheese prices are down $0.1275. The Grade A Swiss prices are unchanged this week.

results.commodity_narrative:
For the start to June, Northeast cheese makers are running through a healthy supply of milk. Cheddar cheese plants are working strong production schedules. In addition, mozzarella and provolone production schedules are fairly full. Cheese inventories remain available for contract/spot demands. Retail sales are good. Several grocery stores are ordering solid amounts of cheese supplies. Foodservice sales are stable at this time. On various market exchanges, cheddar block and barrel prices have slipped downward. Cheese markets are relatively flat.     

In the Northeast, the wholesale cheese prices for both cheddar and Muenster decreased $0.0700. In addition, the process cheese prices are down $0.0325. The Grade A Swiss prices are steady this week. 

The DMN Northeast May 2021 monthly average price for cheddar blocks is $2.3388, compared to $2.3760 one month ago. Processed 5# sliced average price is $2.0831, compared to $1.9631 one month ago.
results.secondary_source_info:
The CME Group May 2021 monthly average price for barrels was $1.6923, compared to $1.7119 a month ago; blocks’ average price was $1.6778, up from $1.7945 a month ago.

This week, a cooperative export assistance program accepted requests for export assistance to sell for 2.4 million pounds (1,104 metric tons) of cheese and 762,800 pounds (346 metric tons) of cream cheese.

results.commodity_narrative:
In the Northeast, milk is aplenty and flowing into cheese operations’ intakes. Cheese makers are working through strong cheddar, mozzarella and provolone production schedules. Manufacturers’ inventory levels are steady for the near term. Retail sales are fairly stable, with some grocers ordering additional supplies. Foodservice cheese sales are steadily soft. Restaurants’ mozzarella and provolone orders are fairly steady. Cheddar cheese spot market activities remain light. There are several buyers not purchasing on the spot market. Cheese markets are bearing a weaker tone, although prices are somewhat settling on various market exchanges.
 
The DMN Northeast January 2021 monthly average price for cheddar blocks is $2.3443, compared to $2.2286 one month ago. Processed 5# sliced average price is $1.8733, compared to $1.7819 one month ago.

In the Northeast, the wholesale cheese prices for both cheddar and Muenster dropped $0.1100. In addition, the process cheese price is down $0.0500. The Grade A Swiss price is steady.
results.secondary_source_info: The CME Group January 2021 monthly average price for barrels was $1.5141, compared to $1.4609 a month ago; blocks’ average price was $1.7470, up from $1.6249 a month ago.

results.commodity_narrative:
Northeastern cheese makers are running strong production schedules. Milk volumes are seasonally abundant in the region. Some Class III plants are operating near or at capacity. Manufacturers’ cheese inventories are slightly increasing, although there are no reports of supplies being burdensome. Spot market activities are somewhat mixed. Foodservice sales are slower. Mozzarella and provolone cheese orders from pizzerias/restaurants are steady to decreased. Retail sales are reportedly steady for the near term. There are reports the Farmers to Families Food Box program has plans to continue and provide dairy products in food boxes. Cheese markets are unsettled. 

The DMN Northeast December 2020 monthly average price for cheddar blocks is $2.2286, compared to $2.8859 one month ago. Processed 5# sliced average price is $1.7819, compared to $2.4082 one month ago.

In the Northeast, the wholesale cheese prices for both cheddar and Muenster increased $0.0100. However, the process cheese price is down $0.0275. The Grade A Swiss price heightened $0.5750 this week.
results.secondary_source_info: The CME Group December 2020 monthly average price for barrels was $1.4609, compared to $1.8437 a month ago; blocks’ average price was $1.6249, down from $2.0521 a month ago.

Some cheese makers are running close to capacity. Cheese markets exemplify a stable to mixed tone. Retail orders are strong, with continual strength in consumers’ cheese demands. Capacity limitations and shutdowns are taking a toll on the restaurant industry. At this time, there is a lot of uncertainty with restaurant/retail sales and educational institutions’ reopening plans that is affecting the cheese market. On the CME Group, block and barrel prices have plummeted compared to last week. Some foodservice sectors have pulled back on ordering. Market participants note throughout the Northeast, numerous restaurants are not serving at full capacity. Cheese makers are working through fairly active production schedules. The Grade A Swiss price is down $0.1050 following the release of the July 2020 Announcement of Class and Component Prices. The Class III skim milk price for July 2020 saw a $3.27 increase from June 2020.

results.commodity_narrative:
Cheese market conditions are unsettled. Foodservice and retail industries continue to be faced with unique situations in their demand cycles. Cheese plants are working through various cheese processes and fortifying for current production needs. Some operations are clearing strong cream loads, taking a toll on cream availability in the area. Milk output has seasonally dropped with hotter weather conditions. Manufacturers’ inventory levels are healthy to tight. On the CME Group, cheddar cheese spot prices are around similar price points compared to last week. Buyers have mixed feelings on current cheese prices. Manufacturers’ orders are also mixed with customers’ demands a bit lower. 

In the Northeast, the wholesale cheese prices for both cheddar and Muenster are down $0.0050. The process cheese prices increased $0.0250. The Grade A Swiss price dropped $0.3625 following the release of the June 2020 Announcement of Class and Component Prices. 

The DMN Northeast June 2020 monthly average price for cheddar blocks is $3.0335, compared to $2.0445 one month ago. Processed 5# sliced average price is $2.5797, compared to $1.7373 one month ago.
results.secondary_source_info:

Eastern cheese makers are working through strong production schedules. Adequate milk supplies are clearing to plants. Inventory levels are balanced to lower in some outlets, as current demands are higher than manufacturers’ current production levels. Mozzarella and provolone interests from restaurants are stable. Several eateries are receiving regular orders to fill consumers’ needs. There are reports foodservice sales have slowed a bit as some operations have filled their pipelines. Market participants report the demand for aged cheddar cheese from local farmers’ markets is healthy. Some buyers have backed off on various market exchanges, due to the currently higher cheese prices, compared to a few weeks ago.

In the Northeast, the wholesale cheese prices for both cheddar and Muenster are up $0.0475. In addition, the process cheese prices increased $0.0975. The Grade A Swiss price is unchanged this week.

The increase in cheese demands are keeping inventory levels balanced to lower. Interests for aged cheddar cheese from specialty retailers and local farmers markets are healthy. results.commodity_narrative:
Milk output is seasonally lower, as the humidity impacts cow comfort in parts of the Northeast. Although milk off the farms, and some bottlers' Class I orders have decreased, milk loads are readily available for cheesemakers' needs. Swiss cheese production is active and interest has strengthened at this time of year. Mozzarella and provolone supplies are steady to growing, but the demand is somewhat slower. Cheddar cheese demand has increased. Cheddar barrel and block spot prices have heightened and spot sales are currently active. Many market participants are speculating if current prices will remain or fall. In the Northeast, the wholesale cheese prices for cheddar and Muenster moved up by $0.0100. Also, the process cheese prices increased by $0.0375. The Grade A Swiss price climbed up $0.1050 following the release of the June 2019 Announcement of Class and Component Prices. However, the Class III skim milk price for June 2019 saw a 43 cents decline.

However, reductions in protein levels are impacting cheese yields. Some facilities are focused on building inventory around the 6-12 months aging process. While inventory levels vary, most are sufficient for filling near-term orders. Export demand is fair, but down 1% from a year ago. In the Northeast, the wholesale cheese price for both cheddar and Muenster shifted higher $0.0375, but process cheese prices moved lower by $0.0050. The Grade A Swiss price moved 13 cents higher last week.

results.commodity_narrative: Northeastern cheese makers report milk production is still increasing in areas of the region. Cheddar cheese processing schedules are running fairly full. Mozzarella and provolone productions are generally steady as milk is readily available for manufacturers' needs. Inventories are growing currently. Cheese demand from grocers is fairly stable. Mozzarella orders are steady to slower as educational institutions are closing for the summer. Cheddar block spot prices are hanging around the low to mid $1.70s, yet cheddar barrel prices have declined on various market exchanges. On the CME Group, cheddar barrel spot trades have been active at this time. The DMN Northeast May 2019 monthly average price for cheddar blocks is $2.2793, compared to $2.2647 one month ago. Processed 5# sliced average price is $2.0141, compared to $1.9580 one month ago. Northeast wholesale cheese prices for cheddar and Muenster increased, $0.0100, however process cheese prices moved down, $0.0625. The Grade A Swiss price is currently steady.

results.commodity_narrative: Northeastern cheese makers report milk production is still increasing in areas of the region. Cheddar cheese processing schedules are running fairly full. Mozzarella and provolone productions are generally steady as milk is readily available for manufacturers' needs. Inventories are growing currently. Cheese demand from grocers is fairly stable. Mozzarella orders are steady to slower as educational institutions are closing for the summer. Cheddar block spot prices are hanging around the low to mid $1.70s, yet cheddar barrel prices have declined on various market exchanges. On the CME Group, cheddar barrel spot trades have been active at this time. The DMN Northeast May 2019 monthly average price for cheddar blocks is $2.2793, compared to $2.2647 one month ago. Processed 5# sliced average price is $2.0141, compared to $1.9580 one month ago. Northeast wholesale cheese prices for cheddar and Muenster increased, $0.0100, however process cheese prices moved down, $0.0625. The Grade A Swiss price is currently steady.

results.commodity_narrative:
Northeastern cheese makers report Class III operations are running fairly full. Milk is around and readily available for production needs. Manufacturers' inventories are increasing at a steady rate. Some facilities will be closed for the holiday. As Memorial Day is nearing, many retailers are advertising holiday discounts. In general, manufacturers' cheese sales are okay to a bit decreased. Food service orders have decreased as many schools in the Northeast are closing for the school year. Cheddar cheese spot prices have simmered compared to recent weeks. On the CME Group, cheddar block prices are a bit increased, yet cheddar barrel prices have softened. Northeast wholesale cheese prices for cheddar and Muenster decreased, $0.0350, and process cheese prices moved down, $0.1050. The Grade A Swiss price is unchanged currently.

Milk loads are keeping manufacturers' intakes fairly full. Cheese makers are clearing all the milk they need to run full production schedules. Cheddar, mozzarella and provolone cheese production is active in the region. Inventories are stable to growing. A few operations have decreased their supplies currently. Cheddar cheese block and barrel spot prices have somewhat strengthened. Spot trading activity is steady to a bit increased. Also, cheddar cheese prices on the GDT event are showing signs of strength. results.commodity_narrative:

Cheddar, mozzarella and provolone cheese production is active in the region. Inventories are stable to growing, but a few operations have decreased their supplies. results.commodity_narrative:
Cheese manufacturers continue to receive heavy milk loads in the Northeast. This week, the region is experiencing dangerous temperatures. Many market participants are preparing for some disruptions in transportation. Although there are some anticipations in driving delays, cheese production schedules are active. Market participants report many operations are running at capacity. Inventories are stable to growing. Pizzerias' cheese orders are strong, as the restaurant owners are gearing up for this Sunday's Super Bowl. Cheddar cheese spot market trading activity is fairly steady. Spot prices have somewhat increased, yet the price spread between the CME Group's cheddar block and barrel cheese is long. Northeast wholesale cheese prices for cheddar and Muenster shifted down by $0.0275, also the process cheese prices moved down by $0.0350. The Grade A Swiss price is unchanged this week.

Some operations will be shut down during the holidays. Pizzerias' holiday orders for Italian cheeses are very good. In the Northeast, wholesale cheese prices for cheddar and Muenster shifted down by $0.0025, and process cheese prices moved lower by $0.0100. However, there are little to no reports of major transportation disruptions or power outages at this time. Cheddar cheese trading activity is steady to quiet this week due to market participants having adequate supplies. Cheddar spot prices are lower on various pricing indices. In the Northeast, wholesale cheese prices for cheddar and Muenster shifted down by $0.0225, however process cheese prices moved up by $0.0225. The Grade A Swiss price is steady this week.

results.commodity_narrative:
Northeast milk production is flat in some areas and slightly increasing in other areas, overall taking a toll on milk availability in the region. In general, milk is in good balance in the Northeast, as loads are securing homes without tolling or cream separation. Milk volumes clearing into Class III are higher this week as other Class' needs are slightly down. Mozzarella and provolone production are fairly steady, and orders are very good from retail and food service sectors. Cheddar cheese production is stable and retail orders are steady to increased as grocers are gearing up for holiday advertisements. Moreover, there are reports of increased cheese consumption in the U.S. than in past years. Cheese supplies are stable in the region, and some cheese makers would like to grow their inventories in the near future. Spot trading is currently lower, and prices fluctuate on various indices this week. In the Northeast, wholesale cheese prices for cheddar and Muenster shifted down by $0.0750, and process cheese prices moved lower by $0.0650. The Grade A Swiss price is steady this week.

results.commodity_narrative:
Cheese production in the Northeast is steady to lower currently, as some operations are closed for scheduled maintenance. In addition, milk availability for Class III is a bit lower, yet some market participants report receiving more milk loads, for cheese processing, than in recent weeks. Mozzarella and provolone processing are active, and customers' orders have increased with the reopening of educational institutions. Swiss cheese production is healthy, but with lower milk volumes, processing is not as vigorous for this time of year. Cheddar cheese production is fairly stable. Cheese inventories are adequate for immediate needs. There are reports of higher demand from retail and food service sectors, as customers are actively purchasing cheese. Spot market trading activity for cheddar barrels is steady to a bit higher. Cheddar barrel spot prices decreased on some pricing indices this week. Cheddar 40-pound block spot activity is steady to lower, and prices are steady to increased. The wholesale prices for cheddar and Muenster declined $0.0125. Also, the process cheese price shifted down $0.0775. The Grade A Swiss price is unchanged this week.

results.commodity_narrative:
Northeast milk production is slightly level on the farms this week. Intermittent hot and humid weather conditions continue to take a toll on cow comfort. Milk volumes clearing into cheese vats are steady to lower, as other Class needs are being met at this time. Mozzarella and provolone cheese production is fairly active. Regular orders have improved with the opening of educational institutions. Fresh cheese supplies are somewhat limited as the demand is keeping inventories stable. There are reports of some operations having adequate supplies of cheese that were made earlier in the year. Trading activity for 40-pound block cheddar cheese is steady to lower. However, barrel cheddar cheese spot trading is steady. Spot prices have decreased and some manufacturers are offering barrels on the spot market. The wholesale prices for cheddar and Muenster declined $0.0500. Also, the process cheese price shifted down $0.1150. The Grade A Swiss price is steady this week.

results.commodity_narrative:
Milk into cheese vats is steady to lower, as milk production continues to decline and bottlers are in high demand for milk supplies. Moreover, the Northeast is facing very hot and humid weather, overall negatively impacting cow comfort. Cheese production is stable to lower. Mozzarella cheese orders are strong as college campuses have reopened for the school year. Consumer retail demand is currently strong as customers are purchasing cheese from grocers at a discount. Manufacturers’ cheese supplies are steady to shorter, as the cheese coming right out of the brine water into packaging is limited. The day after the holiday, cheddar cheese barrel spot market activity was strong. Spot market prices for block and barrel cheddar cheese are steady to higher. The wholesale prices for cheddar and Muenster increased $0.0350. In addition, the process cheese price shifted up $0.0275. The Grade A Swiss price increased $0.0025 this week following the release of the August 2018 Announcement of Class and Component Prices. Additionally, the Class III skim milk price for August 2018 saw a 62 cents incline. The DMN Northeast August 2018 monthly average price for cheddar blocks is $2.1960, compared to $2.3013 one year ago. Processed 5# sliced average price is $1.9210, compared to $1.9870 one year ago.

results.commodity_narrative: Milk production is level to slightly lower this week in the Northeast. Cheese makers in the area report receiving enough milk for full cheese production. The demand for cheese is picking up in the United States. Cheddar and provolone cheese interest in retail and restaurant sectors is fairly stable as orders have increased. Mozzarella demand has strengthened as educational institutions are resupplying their inventories for the new school year. Cheese stocks are steady to higher, as cheese production in the Northeast is active. Spot trading is steady to light as many market participants are working through contracts and are seeing where the spot prices lead. The wholesale prices for cheddar and Muenster increased $0.0250. However, the process cheese price is unchanged. The Grade A Swiss price increased $0.0800 following the release of the July 2018 Announcement of Class and Component Prices. Overall, the Class III skim milk price for July 2018 saw a 64 cent decline. The DMN Northeast July 2018 monthly average price for cheddar blocks is $2.1317, compared to $2.1900 one year ago. Processed 5# sliced average price is $1.7167, compared to $1.8060 one year ago.

results.commodity_narrative: Milk volumes are available in the Northeast for strong cheese processing. Cheese makers report they are clearing milk loads into vats at close to plant capacity levels to handle milk supplies before the holiday. However, some operations will be open all week as production schedules are full. Cheddar cheese inventories are stable to increasing. The demand for cheddar in the retail sector is steady to increased this week, as the July 4 holiday increased grocers’ cheese advertisements. Mozzarella and provolone supplies are steady to growing as interest is somewhat slower currently. Spot market conditions have gained some strength back this week as prices are higher, yet with much concern over the demand for U.S. exports and the shortened trading week, buyers are taking a wait and see approach to the current market. The process cheese price declined $0.0425. Also, the wholesale prices for cheddar and Muenster decreased $0.0375. The Grade A Swiss price is unchanged. The DMN Northeast June 2018 monthly average price for cheddar blocks is $2.1888, compared to $2.2350 one year ago. Processed 5# sliced average price is $1.8551, compared to $1.8231 one year ago.

Italian cheese inventories are long and increasing, waiting for the school year to pick up in August. The recent trade news from China have concerned some contacts about how the cheese market will be affected. The spot market activity is bearish, with block and barrel prices dropping significantly moving into the week on the CME, and the price gap increasing. The process cheese price decreased $0.0075. Moreover, the wholesale prices for cheddar and Muenster increased $0.0225. The Grade A Swiss price is unchanged.

results.commodity_narrative:
Milk volumes in the Northeast are heavy and putting some pressure on cheese plants. Some operations’ production schedules are shortened for maintenance and their operations are not able to take in as much milk this week. Overall, cheese facilities are at lower to full capacity. Cheddar cheese processing is stable to a tad lower as production needs are decreased. Provolone and mozzarella production are steady and strong as milk is readily available. General cheese supplies are steady to growing. The demand for cheddar and mozzarella is steady to somewhat slowed down, however sliced provolone demand is currently stable. Spot market activity is steady to slightly increased as cheese barrels had some uptick in interest. With some international markets changing trading regulations, many market participants anticipate a change in general market cheese prices. The process cheese price decreased $0.0225. Moreover, the wholesale price for cheddar and Muenster declined $0.0125. The Grade A Swiss price is unchanged.

results.commodity_narrative:
Northeast cheese makers are receiving high milk levels into their intakes. Production schedules are running at to near capacity. Cheddar production is strong and market participants report they are clearing extra milk loads. Cheddar cheese interest from retail sectors is fairly steady. Mozzarella and provolone production are steady as milk is available for production needs. The demand for contract orders of provolone sliced cheese is stable. Mozzarella orders are steady to slow as educational institutions are closing for the summer. Overall cheese inventories are stable to increasing. Cheddar block and barrel cheese trading activities and pricing are mixed. Some pricing indices’ prices and activity are higher and active, although other spot trades and prices are lower. The process cheese price decreased $0.0125. In addition, the wholesale price for cheddar and Muenster declined $0.0200. The Grade A Swiss price increased $0.0925 following the release of the May 2018 Announcement of Class and Component Prices. Additionally, the Class III skim milk price for May 2018 saw a 32 cents increase. The DMN Northeast May 2018 monthly average price for cheddar blocks is $2.2388, compared to $2.1890 one year ago. Processed 5# sliced average price is $1.9476, compared to $1.8390 one year ago.

Major roadways were closed, but there have not been many reports of milk transportation delays. Northeast cheese production is close to full capacity as more available milk loads are being cleared into intakes. Inventories are in pretty decent shape as manufacturers report mozzarella and provolone retail orders are good. Domestic cheddar cheese spot prices are fairly steady and cheddar barrel spot sales seem to have more activity this week compared to past weeks and some export cheddar trading prices have increased. Cheddar barrels seemed to garner more interest than cheddar blocks this week. The wholesale price for cheddar and Muenster increased $0.0625. In addition, the process cheese price shifted higher $0.0225. The Grade A Swiss price is unchanged. National Retail Report-Dairy, for April 13-19, 2018, noted the U.S. weighted average advertised price for 8 ounce cheese block was $2.06, up 19 cents from the previous week, but down 26 cents from last year. The U.S. weighted average advertised price of 8 ounce cheese shreds was $2.28, an increase of 35 cents from last week, but down 3 cents from a year ago. Northeast region’s weighted average advertised price for 8 ounce cheese blocks was $2.57, 51 cents above the U.S. average, with a regional price range of $1.99-$3.00. The average price for 8 oz. cheese shreds was $2.59, 31 cents above the national average, with prices ranging $1.99-$3.00. In the Southeast region, the average price for 8 oz. cheese blocks was $2.04, 2 cents below the average U.S. price, with a regional price range of $1.67-$2.50. The average price for 8 oz. shreds was $2.63, 35 cents above the U.S. average, with prices ranging $1.67-$3.00.

results.commodity_narrative: Milk volumes are plentiful in the Northeast region as the spring flush is just starting in some areas. Cheese processing is strong as cheese vats are full with milk supplies. Orders are steady from food service sectors and inventories are fairly stable. Spot activity for cheese barrels has picked up along with the price in some indices. The wholesale price for cheddar and Muenster increased $0.0200. However, the process cheese price shifted lower $0.0325. The Grade A Swiss price decreased $0.1600. However, the Class III skim milk price for March 2018 saw a 56 cents increase from the previous month following the release of the March 2018 Announcement of Class and Component Prices. This week, a cooperative export assistance program accepted requests for export assistance to sell 1.250 million pounds (567 metric tons) of cheese. National Retail Report-Dairy, for April 6-12, 2018, noted the U.S. weighted average advertised price for 8 ounce cheese block was $1.87, down 15 cents from the previous week and down 24 cents from last year. The U.S. weighted average advertised price of 8 ounce cheese shreds was $1.93, a decrease of 13 cents from last week and down 30 cents from a year ago. Northeast region’s weighted average advertised price for 8 ounce cheese blocks was $2.21, 34 cents above the U.S. average, with a regional price range of $0.99-$2.99. The average price for 8 oz. cheese shreds was $2.15, 22 cents above the national average, with prices ranging $0.99-$2.99. In the Southeast region, the average price for 8 oz. cheese blocks was $1.76, 11 cents below the average U.S. price, with a regional price range of $0.99-$2.00. The average price for 8 oz. shreds was $1.88, 5 cents below the U.S. average, with prices ranging $0.99-$2.50.

results.commodity_narrative: Northeast market participants report milk production is slightly increasing, as warmer weather is trying to make its way to the region. With bottling orders still down, available milk loads are clearing into more manufacturing intakes. Cheese processing is steady and contract orders are fairly firm. Pricing indices are mixed, yet cheese spot sales are quite moderate this week. The wholesale price for cheddar and Muenster decreased $0.0225. In addition, the process cheese price shifted lower $0.0425. The Grade A Swiss price is steady. The DMN Northeast March 2018 monthly average price for cheddar blocks is $2.1559, compared to $2.0529 one year ago. Processed 5# sliced average price is $1.8811, compared to $1.8099 one year ago. The CME Group March 2018 monthly average price for barrels was $1.5071, compared to $1.4072 a year ago; blocks’ average price was $1.5614, compared to $1.4342 a year ago. This week, a cooperative export assistance program accepted 11 requests for export assistance to sell 2.017 million pounds (915 metric tons) of cheese. National Retail Report-Dairy, for March 30-April 5, 2018, noted the U.S. weighted average advertised price for 8 ounce cheese block was $2.02, down 15 cents from the previous week and down 17 cents from last year. The U.S. weighted average advertised price of 8 ounce cheese shreds was $2.06, an increase of 3 cents from last week, but down 14 cents from a year ago. Northeast region’s weighted average advertised price for 8 ounce cheese blocks was $1.91, 11 cents below the U.S. average, with a regional price range of $0.99-$2.00. The average price for 8 oz. cheese shreds was $2.03, 3 cents below the national average, with prices ranging $0.99-$3.00. In the Southeast region, the average price for 8 oz. cheese blocks was $1.95, 7 cents below the average U.S. price, with a regional price range of $1.66-$3.00. The average price for 8 oz. shreds was $1.96, 10 cents below the U.S. average, with prices ranging $1.66-$2.50.
results.methodology: Information for the period April 2 - 6, 2018, issued weekly

results.commodity_narrative: Northeast milk production is increasing, mainly allowing more available milk for manufacturing needs. Class I orders are lower in the East, thus milk is clearing heavily into Class III intakes. Cheese production is strong and manufacturers report orders are fairly good. Spot sales for cheese block and barrel are mixed, as some cheese markets report slow trades. The wholesale price for cheddar and Muenster decreased $0.0075. In addition, the process cheese price shifted lower $0.0025. The Grade A Swiss price is unchanged. At Tuesday’s CME Group trading, daily cash prices saw barrels close at $1.5000, down $0.0175, and blocks closed at $1.5450, an increase of $0.0025 from last Tuesday. National Retail Report-Dairy, for March 23-29, 2018, noted the U.S. weighted average advertised price for 8 ounce cheese block was $2.17, down 9 cents from the previous week, but up 5 cents from last year. The U.S. weighted average advertised price of 8 ounce cheese shreds was $2.03, a decrease of 20 cents from last week and down 8 cents from a year ago. Northeast region’s weighted average advertised price for 8 ounce cheese blocks was $2.30, 13 cents above the U.S. average, with a regional price range of $0.99-$3.00. The average price for 8 oz. cheese shreds was $2.02, 1 cent below the national average, with prices ranging $0.99-$2.99. In the Southeast region, the average price for 8 oz. cheese blocks was $2.03, 14 cents below the average U.S. price, with a regional price range of $1.66-$3.00. The average price for 8 oz. shreds was $1.93, 10 cents below the U.S. average, with prices ranging $1.66-$2.50.
results.secondary_source_info: COLD STORAGE: According to NASS, U.S. stocks of total natural cheese as of February 2018 totaled 1.3 billion pounds, 3 percent more than the previous month and up 7 percent from a year ago. Swiss cheese totaled 27.9 million pounds, 3 percent more than a year ago, but decreased 3 percent from last month. In New England, stocks of American cheese totaled 65.0 million pounds, 1 percent lower than February 2017, but 3 percent higher from January 2018.

The average price for 8 oz. cheese shreds was $2.20, the same price as the  national average, with prices ranging $1.29-$3.00. results.commodity_narrative:
Northeastern U.S. Cheese Commentary:
Northeast cheese production is busy as milk continues to clear into vats. Milk availability is steady to tight as some cheese makers report they are receiving just enough loads for scheduled production levels. With the upcoming Super Bowl, domestic cheddar cheese block sales are up. Spot sale cheese trading activities are stable to light as prices on some indices are solid, however some market participants are content with their orders and do not need to purchase immediate loads. The Northeast wholesale cheddar and Muenster prices decreased $0.0125, but the process cheese price increased $0.0225. The Grade A Swiss price is steady. This week, a cooperative export assistance program accepted 25 requests for export assistance to sell 4.365 million pounds (1,982 metric tons) of cheese. At Tuesday’s CME Group trading, daily cash prices saw barrels closed at $1.3200, down $0.0450, and blocks closed at $1.4625, decreased $0.0975 from last Tuesday. The DMN National Retail Report-Dairy, for January 26-February 1, 2018, noted the U.S. weighted average advertised price for 8 ounce cheese block was $2.28, decreased 21 cents from the previous week, but up 23 cents from last year. The U.S. weighted average advertised price of 8 ounce cheese shreds was $2.27, down 13 cents from last week, but up 8 cents from a year ago. Northeast region’s weighted average advertised price for 8 ounce cheese blocks was $2.11, 17 cents below the U.S. average, with a regional price range of $1.67-$3.50. The Southeast region’s average price for 8 oz. cheese blocks was $2.40, 12 cents above the average U.S. price, with a regional price range of $1.99-$3.50. The Northeast average price for 8 oz. cheese shreds was $2.37, up 10 cents from the U.S. average price, with a regional price range of $1.88-$3.00. In the Southeast, the average price for 8 oz. shreds was $2.27, same price as the U.S. average, with prices ranging $1.99-$2.50. COLD STORAGE: According to NASS, U.S. stocks of total natural cheese as of December 31, 2017 totaled 1.3 billion pounds, 2 percent higher than the previous month, and up 7 percent from a year ago. Swiss cheese totaled 26.4 million pounds, 9 percent higher than a year ago, and up 6 percent from last month. In New England, stocks of American cheese totaled 67.7 million pounds, 6 percent higher than December 2016 and 7 percent higher than November 2017.
